subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Explain the effect of increasing temperature and increasing carbon dioxide concentration on the rate of photosynthesis shown in Figure 7.
answer: Both raise the rate (faster particles and enzymes; more CO₂ as substrate) until it plateaus when another factor limits — Increasing the temperature while keeping the carbon dioxide concentration constant increases the rate of photosynthesis (and the converse for carbon dioxide at constant temperature); increasing the temperature increases the movement — the kinetic energy — of the particles, or the rate of enzyme activity, or the frequency of collisions; increasing the carbon dioxide concentration increases the concentration of the substrate; and all the rates plateau at a certain point because another factor becomes limiting. ('Because light is limiting' is not accepted; chlorophyll is.)

html:
Photosynthesis investigations often use a light source. The spreading out of light from a source obeys the inverse square law, which links light intensity to distance from the light source.

Which of the following shows the inverse square law? Tick one box.
answer: light intensity ∝ 1 ÷ distance²
choices: light intensity ∝ 1 ÷ distance<sup>2</sup> | light intensity ∝ distance<sup>2</sup> | 1 ÷ (light intensity)<sup>2</sup> ∝ distance<sup>2</sup> | 1 ÷ (light intensity)<sup>2</sup> ∝ 1 ÷ distance<sup>2</sup>

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Cancer is caused by changes in cells that result in uncontrolled cell division.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Before a cell begins to divide, its DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome.

Describe one other change that occurs in a cell before the cell begins to divide.
answer: Any one: the cell grows, or makes more sub-cellular structures such as mitochondria or ribosomes — Any one of: the cell or its sub-cellular structures grow; the number of sub-cellular structures increases; the number of mitochondria increases; the number of ribosomes increases. The nucleus is not accepted, and neither is anything that happens as the cell divides.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 shows some of the stages of cell division, with the fibres attaching to the replicated chromosomes at stage 1 and pulling them to each end of the cell.

Some cancer drugs prevent cell division. Drug X prevents the fibres from attaching to the replicated chromosomes in stage 1.

Explain why a cell cannot complete division when affected by drug X.
answer: The chromosomes cannot be pulled by the fibres to each end of the cell; so the nucleus cannot divide — two genetically identical cells cannot be formed.
examiner_note: Figure 9 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give the reason why a drug that stops cell division helps to treat cancer.
answer: The tumour cannot grow, proliferate or spread — it stops secondary tumours forming (metastasis). 'It stops uncontrolled cell division' is ignored, and 'the tumour cannot become malignant' is not accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
New cancer drugs are tested in clinical trials. Preclinical testing happens before clinical trials.

What is involved in preclinical testing of drugs? Tick one box.
answer: Testing the drugs on live tissues in a laboratory
choices: Testing the drugs for side effects | Testing the drugs on live tissues in a laboratory | Testing the drugs to find the optimum dose | Testing the drugs with chemicals in a laboratory

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Evolution of new species occurs by mutation and natural selection.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: What is a mutation?
answer: A change in the DNA — in the base code or nucleotide sequence, in a base, in a gene or allele, in part of a chromosome, in the number of chromosomes, or in the genetic material. 'Genetic information' and 'variation' are ignored, and so is any reference to amino acids or proteins.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe the process of natural selection.
answer: Variation; the best adapted survive and reproduce, passing on favourable alleles — Any three of: there is variation between members of a species; the better adapted survive (survival of the fittest); the survivors reproduce; and they pass on the favourable alleles or genes. An answer given in terms of a worked example is accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Which scientists suggested the theory of evolution by natural selection?

Tick one box.
answer: Alfred Wallace and Charles Darwin
choices: Alexander Fleming and Carl Woese | Alfred Wallace and Alexander Fleming | Alfred Wallace and Charles Darwin | Charles Darwin and Carl Woese

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The hoverfly and the wasp are insects with bright yellow and black markings. Figure 1 is a photograph of a hoverfly beside a wasp, showing that the two have a very similar pattern of yellow and black bands.

The wasp has a sting to defend itself against predators. The hoverfly does not have a sting. Hoverflies and wasps live in the same habitat.

Explain how having yellow and black markings helps the hoverfly survive.
answer: It looks like a wasp; predators avoid wasps so as not to be stung, so they do not attack or eat the hoverfly — the pattern of markings is similar; a predator avoids wasps so that it does not get stung; so the predator does not attack or eat the hoverfly. ('The predator thinks it is a wasp' is ignored.)
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Peat bogs are estimated to contain twice as much carbon as all the world’s forests.

Figure 2 shows a section through part of a peat bog: moss and a sundew plant grow on the surface, layer A lies just below the surface, and layer B lies below layer A.

Layer A contains a lot of air.

Layer B:

  • contains the dead remains of plants
  • has a low pH
  • contains very little oxygen
  • contains carbon dioxide and methane.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain why most of the dead remains of plants in layer B do not decay.
answer: There is a lack of oxygen for aerobic respiration; so less or no energy is released; in the microorganisms — the bacteria, fungi and decomposers. The alternative route also scores three: the low pH denatures enzymes, so there are fewer reactions and less energy released, in the microorganisms. Respiration in the dead plants is not accepted, and neither is energy being 'produced' or 'made'.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The peat bog in Figure 2 is a stable community.

The moss produces biomass at a rate of 340 g/m2/year.

What is the approximate biomass of the moss that becomes biomass in primary consumers?

Tick one box.
answer: 34 g/m²/year — about 10% of the biomass at one trophic level is transferred to the next
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The sundew plant shown in Figure 2 has leaves with sticky hairs that trap and digest insects.

Digestion of the insects releases phosphates and simple compounds of nitrogen that are used by the sundew plant.

What substance can the sundew plant make using the phosphates?

Tick one box.
answer: DNA

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
What substance can the sundew plant make using the nitrogen?

Tick one box.
answer: Protein
choices: Fatty acid | Glucose | Lactic acid | Protein

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Humans have destroyed large areas of peat bog to collect peat.

The peat provides fuel and provides compost for gardeners to use.

The peat comes from layer B in Figure 2.

Layer B:

  • contains the dead remains of plants
  • has a low pH
  • contains very little oxygen
  • contains carbon dioxide and methane.

Figure 3 shows the removal of peat from a peat bog: blocks of peat cut from the bog and stacked.

Explain how the destruction of peat bogs and the use of peat affects the temperature of the Earth’s atmosphere.
answer: It increases: carbon dioxide is released from the bog and by burning or decay of the peat, and methane from the bog — global warming, heat energy trapped; because carbon dioxide is released from the peat bog; because carbon dioxide is produced by burning or by the decay of the peat; and because methane is released from the peat bog. That there are fewer plants left to take carbon dioxide in for photosynthesis is also allowed.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Frogs are animals that lay their eggs in water. The eggs hatch as tadpoles.

Students investigated the number of tadpoles in a pond for 8 weeks.

This is the method used.

  1. Collect 10 dm3 of pond water in a bucket.
  2. Count the number of tadpoles collected.
  3. Put the tadpoles back into the pond.
  4. Repeat steps 1 to 3 another three times in different parts of the pond.
  5. Repeat steps 1 to 4 at intervals for 8 weeks.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Suggest one improvement to the method.
answer: Any one: more or bigger samples, more often, at the same time of day, at random places — Any one of: collect more samples each time; collect samples more frequently; use a bigger bucket or sample; do not return the tadpoles until after the fourth sample (any method that avoids double counting); sample at the same time of day; randomise the collecting positions; collect at a range of depths; use standardised sweeps with a net instead of a bucket.

Calculate value X.

Complete Figure 4 to show how the total number of tadpoles changed over the 8 weeks.

You should:

  • label the x-axis
  • use a suitable scale for the x-axis
  • plot the data for the total numbers of tadpoles from Table 1
  • draw a line of best fit.

Figure 4 is a graph grid: the y-axis is labelled ‘Total number of tadpoles’ from 0 to 70; the x-axis is blank.

Draw a curved line of best fit (1 mark) — a line drawn point to point is ignored.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
After 0 weeks, no more tadpoles hatched in the pond.

Calculate the percentage of the tadpoles that would still be found in the pond at 4 weeks compared with 0 weeks. Use information from Figure 4.
answer: About 36.7%. Read the values at 0 and 4 weeks off your own line of best fit — 60 and about 22 (1 mark); 22 ÷ 60 × 100 (1 mark); 36.7, and 37 or 36.6… are accepted (1 mark). Any calculation consistent with your own line scores. If no line was drawn, 60 and 24 taken from the table are allowed for full marks.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
After 4 weeks many of the tadpoles had died.

Suggest two reasons why the tadpoles died.
answer: Any two: disease, predators, lack of food, low oxygen, a change in temperature or pH, pollution — Any two of: disease or a named pathogen; being eaten by predators; lack of food (competition for food); low oxygen concentration in the water (eutrophication); a change in temperature; a change in pH; some of the pond dried out (lack of space); a toxic chemical such as sewage or fertiliser. Unqualified 'competition', 'pollution' and 'waste' are ignored.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the effect of gravity on the growth of bean seedlings.

The student put ink marks on the root of each bean seedling.

Figure 5 shows a bean seedling with ink marks at even spacings along its root.

The student set up apparatus A and apparatus B.

Figure 6 shows both sets of apparatus. In apparatus A the seedlings, surrounded by damp blotting paper, are held still with their roots horizontal. In apparatus B the same arrangement is on a slowly turning wheel (a clinostat).

The student left both sets of apparatus in a dark cupboard for 24 hours.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Give the reason why the student placed both sets of apparatus in the dark.
answer: To prevent the direction of the light affecting the results or the growth of the roots — to prevent phototropism, so that only gravity affects the growth.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
What are two reasons for surrounding the seedlings with damp blotting paper?

Tick two boxes.
answer: To prevent water affecting the direction of root growth; and to provide enough water for root growth.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.
choices: To prevent photosynthesis in the roots | To prevent the growth of mould on the roots | To prevent water affecting the direction of root growth | To provide enough water for root growth | To provide the roots with mineral ions

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Apparatus B is a control.

Explain why apparatus B is needed.
answer: To compare with A: it shows gravity caused A’s results, as in B gravity acted equally in all directions — to see the difference between them; so that it shows that gravity caused the results in apparatus A, because gravity acted equally in all directions in B, cancelling out its one-sided effect.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 7 shows one seedling from apparatus A at the start of the investigation and after 24 hours.

The drawing of the seedling after 24 hours is not complete.

Complete Figure 7 to show:

  • the appearance of the root after 24 hours
  • the ink marks on the root after 24 hours.
answer: The root bent downwards and longer, with the ink marks spread out in the bend — Draw the root bending downwards (1); draw it longer than it was at the start (1); and show the ink marks spread out in the bent region (1). Marks spread out before the bend are not accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe how a root from apparatus B would look different from the root you drew in Question 04.4.
answer: It would be horizontal — growing straight out, not bent at all.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Auxin is a plant hormone.

Explain how auxin causes the results in apparatus A.
answer: More auxin collects on the lower side, so the upper side grows faster than the lower side — There is an uneven distribution of auxin — more of it on the lower side; so the upper side grows faster than the lower (or the lower side grows more slowly than the upper). 'More auxin on the upper side' is ignored.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Farmers can use plant hormones to control the growth of plants.

Give two uses of auxin.
answer: Any two: weed killer, rooting powder, tissue culture, inhibiting lateral buds — Any two of: as weed killers; in rooting powders, to grow plants from cuttings; to promote growth in tissue culture; to inhibit lateral buds.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A farmer sprayed an apple tree with gibberellin.

Suggest two reasons why the farmer sprayed the apple tree with gibberellin.
answer: Any two: to make it flower, for more fruit, for bigger fruit — Any two of: to promote, start or force flowering (to grow more flowers); to get more fruit; to get bigger fruits. The idea of the fruits ripening at the same time is also allowed, and if neither 'more' nor 'bigger' is given, a bigger yield of apples scores one.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The human body has two coordination systems:

  • the nervous system
  • the endocrine system.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Two students investigated human reaction time.

Student A held a metre rule above student B’s hand.

Student A then released the metre rule and student B caught the rule as quickly as possible.

Figure 8 shows the method used: the rule hangs vertically with its lower end between the open thumb and finger of student B.

Suggest two ways to improve the students’ method for measuring human reaction time.
answer: Any two: same start position, a millimetre scale, repeat for a mean, rest the hand on a table — Any two of: use the same starting position of the ruler each time (or any other control variable); use a more precise scale — a ruler with millimetres; repeat and calculate a mean, or repeat and eliminate anomalies; convert the distance into a time; rest student B's hand or arm on a table.
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Student B’s reaction is coordinated by the nervous system.

Give two ways that coordination by the endocrine system is different from coordination by the nervous system.
answer: Any two: hormones in the blood, not neurones; chemical, not electrical; slower; lasts longer — Any two of: the endocrine system sends hormones via the blood rather than along neurones; it is chemical rather than electrical transmission; it is slower; its effects are longer-lasting. The answers must be comparative.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 shows endocrine glands in a female: gland A is labelled in the neck and gland B is labelled behind the stomach.

Name one hormone produced by gland A.
answer: Thyroxine (not 'thyroxide'; TSH and TRH are ignored)
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Name one hormone produced by gland B.
answer: Insulin or glucagon
examiner_note: Artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The adrenal gland produces the hormone adrenaline.

Describe two effects of adrenaline on the human body.
answer: Any two: faster heart rate, faster breathing, more oxygen and glucose to cells, more respiration — Any two of: increases the heart rate (blood flow); increases the breathing rate; increases oxygen delivery to the cells and tissues; increases glucose delivery to them; increases respiration or metabolism — energy release; increases sweating. Dilation of the pupils, vasoconstriction in the skin and digestive system, vasodilation in the muscles and brain, raised blood pressure, raised blood glucose and slowed digestion are all accepted. 'Prepares for fight or flight' alone scores one.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Hormones can be used for controlling human reproduction.

Explain the use of hormones in:

  • contraception
  • the treatment of infertility.
answer: Contraception: hormones stop FSH and LH. Infertility: FSH and LH make eggs mature and release — Level-marked out of 6, and Level 3 needs both halves. Contraception: oestrogen and progesterone, or progesterone alone, inhibit the production of FSH — so no follicle or egg matures and there is no egg to fertilise — and inhibit LH, so there is no ovulation. The methods include the oral pill, an injection, an implant, a skin patch and a hormonal IUD or IUS. Infertility: FSH stimulates several eggs to mature, increasing the number available; LH stimulates ovulation and lets the eggs be collected from the ovary, which increases the chance of fertilising one, as in IVF where an embryo is then inserted into the uterus; progesterone maintains the uterus lining and increases the chance of implantation.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Some human disorders are inherited.

Polydactyly is an inherited disorder.

  • A person with polydactyly has extra fingers or toes.
  • Polydactyly is caused by a dominant allele.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: What is a dominant allele?
answer: An allele that is always expressed — that shows in the phenotype even when the recessive allele is also present, that is expressed in the heterozygote, or that is expressed when only one copy is present. 'Stronger' is ignored.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 10 shows the inheritance of polydactyly in one family.

Key: filled square = male who has polydactyly; open square = male who does not have polydactyly; filled circle = female who has polydactyly; open circle = female who does not have polydactyly.

In questions 06.2 and 06.3, use the following symbols:

D = allele for having polydactyly
d = allele for not having polydactyly.

Person 1 is heterozygous.

Explain how Figure 10 shows that person 1 is heterozygous.
answer: Person 1 has a D (affected) and a d, because child 5 is dd — Person 1 has polydactyly, so must have a D (a dominant allele); and person 1 has a child, person 5, who does not have polydactyly — person 5 must be dd, so must have inherited a d from person 1. An annotated genetic diagram scores both marks.

html:
Key: filled square = male who has polydactyly; open square = male who does not have polydactyly; filled circle = female who has polydactyly; open circle = female who does not have polydactyly.

Persons 6 and 7 are expecting a fourth child.

A doctor states that the probability of having a child with polydactyly is 0.5

Explain how the doctor determined this probability.

You should:

  • draw a Punnett square diagram
  • give the genotype of person 6 and the genotype of person 7
  • identify all the offspring that will have polydactyly.
answer: Person 6 is Dd, person 7 is dd; the square gives Dd, Dd, dd, dd, so 2 in 4 (0.5) have polydactyly — Person 6 has polydactyly and has children without it, so she is Dd and her gametes are D and d (1 mark) — Person 7 does not have polydactyly, so he is dd and both his gametes are d (1 mark). The Punnett square gives Dd, Dd, dd, dd (1 mark, and it must follow from the gametes given). Two of the four are Dd, which is half, so the probability of polydactyly is 0.5 (1 mark, awarded only if the square is right).

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Cystic fibrosis (CF) is another inherited disorder, caused by a mutation in a gene called CFTR. For the CFTR gene, one allele in every 50 in the UK population is the cystic fibrosis allele.

Explain why only one person in 2500 in the UK population has cystic fibrosis.
answer: CF is recessive, so it needs two CF alleles: <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>50</sub> × <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>50</sub> = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2500</sub> — The CF allele is recessive; so to have CF a person must have two CF alleles; the chance of any one allele being the CF allele is 1 in 50; and the chance of having two is <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>50</sub> × <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>50</sub> = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2500</sub>. ('50 × 50 = 2500' on its own is ignored — it is the multiplication of the two probabilities that earns the mark.)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Farmers can increase the growth rate of farm animals by controlling the animals’ diets.

A farmer has 1000 chickens.

  • The farmer feeds the chickens on seeds from maize plants.
  • 1 hectare of land produces 16.4 tonnes of maize seeds.
  • The maize seeds have an energy content of 16 MJ per kg.
  • Chickens can use 80% of the energy in maize seeds.
  • Each chicken needs 46 MJ of energy to grow to full size.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Calculate the area of land needed to provide enough energy from maize seeds for 1000 chickens to grow to full size.

Give your answer in m2.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

1 hectare = 10 000 m2
1 tonne = 1000 kg
answer: 2190 m² — The chickens need 1000 × 46 = 46 000 MJ. One hectare gives 16.4 tonnes = 16 400 kg of seed, worth 16 400 × 16 = 262 400 MJ, of which the chickens can use 80% = 209 920 MJ. So 46 000 ÷ 209 920 = 0.2191… hectares, and × 10 000 = 2191.3 m², which to 3 significant figures is 2190 m². (The scheme's other route is the same sum the other way round: each kilogram of seed gives the chickens 16 × 0.8 = 12.8 MJ, so 46 000 ÷ 12.8 = 3593.75 kg of seed is needed, and 3593.75 ÷ 16 400 × 10 000 = 2191.3 m².)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Another farmer produced 4200 kg of maize seeds in a field. The farmer fed the maize to 1000 chickens. At full size, the mean mass of one chicken was 2.2 kg.

Figure 11 is a blank grid with a zero line up the middle.

Complete Figure 11 to show a pyramid of biomass for the food chain from the maize seeds to 1000 chickens. You should label the x-axis and use a suitable scale.
answer: Bars centred on the zero line, x-axis 'Biomass in kg': maize 4200 kg at the bottom, chickens 1000 × 2.2 = 2200 kg above — Label the x-axis 'Biomass in kg' and label the two bars 'maize' and 'chickens' (1 mark). Draw the maize bar at 4200 kg and the chickens bar at 1000 × 2.2 = 2200 kg, with the chickens above the maize (1 mark; half a small square of tolerance, and the height of the bars is ignored).

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Calculate the ratio of chicken biomass to maize seed biomass. Use data from Question 07.2. Give your answer in its simplest form.
answer: 11 : 21 — The chicken biomass is 2200 kg and the maize is 4200 kg, so the ratio is 2200 : 4200 (1 mark), which simplifies to 11 : 21 (1 mark). 0.5238… : 1 and 1 : 1.9 are also accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Chickens can use 80% of the biomass from the maize seeds they eat for respiration and growth.

What happens to the remaining 20% of the biomass in the maize seeds?
answer: It is lost via egestion — in the faeces. Urine, excretion and 'not digested' are ignored; respiration, 'not eaten', movement and heat are not accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Protein is an important part of a chicken’s diet. Proteins contain 20 different types of amino acid; a chicken can make many of them from other substances in the diet, but the essential amino acids are the ones it cannot make and must be given. Maize seeds contain protein but the proportion of some essential amino acids is low, so scientists have produced Quality Protein Maize (QPM). Table 2 compares the proportions of seven essential amino acids in the two.

Amino acidNormal maize (g/kg)Quality protein maize, QPM (g/kg)
Leucine122.288.1
Lysine28.941.9
Methionine19.918.1
Phenylalanine49.440.9
Threonine34.536.5
Tryptophan7.316.3
Valine45.951.2

Which amino acids are found in significantly higher proportions in the QPM seeds? Tick one box.
answer: Lysine and tryptophan — lysine rises from 28.9 to 41.9 and tryptophan from 7.3 to 16.3, where threonine and valine barely move
choices: Lysine and tryptophan | Lysine and valine | Threonine and tryptophan | Threonine and valine

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Table 2 shows that 1 kg of QPM contains less leucine than 1 kg of normal maize.

Suggest why a diet containing less leucine does not slow down the growth of chickens.
answer: Chickens need only a low amount of leucine for growth — chicken proteins contain a low proportion of leucine. 'Leucine is not needed for growth' is not accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Conditions inside and outside of the human body often change.

Homeostasis helps the human body to survive changing conditions.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain what is meant by the term ‘homeostasis’.
answer: Keeping internal conditions constant, so they stay at the optimum for cells and enzyme action — keeping them the same; so that the conditions are optimum for the cells and for enzyme activity.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The kidneys have an important role in homeostasis.

Describe what happens to glucose, protein and urea in the kidneys.
answer: Glucose and urea filtered out, protein not; all glucose reabsorbed, urea leaves in urine — Glucose and urea are filtered out of the blood; protein is not filtered out of the blood; all of the glucose is reabsorbed back into the blood; and the urea is mostly not reabsorbed — it passes out in the urine.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain how ADH affects the production and concentration of urine by the kidneys.
answer: High ADH increases water reabsorption from the kidney tubules, so the urine is more concentrated and smaller in volume — it increases the permeability to water; the reabsorption happens from the kidney tubules; so ADH increases the concentration of the urine; and decreases its volume. The converse for a low level of ADH is accepted throughout.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Glyphosate is a herbicide used in agriculture.

Soya bean plants have been genetically modified (GM) to be resistant to glyphosate.

A farmer can increase the yield of soya beans by:

  • growing GM soya bean plants
  • spraying glyphosate on the field.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain how the use of GM soya bean plants and glyphosate can increase the yield of soya beans.
answer: Fewer weeds, so less competition, so more photosynthesis and more glucose for growth — Level-marked out of 6. The glyphosate kills the weeds but does not harm the GM soya; so there is less competition for light, water, mineral ions and space; more light and water means more photosynthesis and so more glucose. The extra glucose goes to respiration for energy, cellulose for cell walls, starch for stored energy, protein for cell structure and lipids for energy storage in the beans. The extra water gives turgor and support, transport, a medium for reactions and hydrolysis of stored substances. More magnesium makes chlorophyll, more nitrate makes amino acids and proteins, more phosphate makes DNA.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Suggest two reasons why some people are concerned about the use of GM soya bean plants.

Do not refer to ethical concerns or religion in your answer.
answer: Any two: unknown effects of eating it, genes spreading to wild plants, less biodiversity, cost — Any two of: the effects on animals or humans of eating them are not known; the gene may be transferred to other, wild plants; they reduce biodiversity; the seed costs the farmer more, or the product costs the consumer more; they may affect the flavour of the product. Unqualified 'cost' is ignored.

answer: 7⁄12 < 2⁄3 < 3⁄4 (or any three in this order: 7⁄12, 2⁄3, 3⁄4, 7⁄9) — in thirty-sixths they are 21, 24, 27 and 28, so 7⁄12 < 2⁄3 < 3⁄4 < 7⁄9; 3⁄4 and 7⁄9 are the close pair.

name: Angles in Polygons
subject: Maths
html: What do the angles in a pentagon add up to?
answer: 540° — each extra side adds another triangle, another 180°: 360 + 180 = 540.

name: Angles in Polygons
subject: Maths
html: What do the angles in a hexagon add up to?
answer: 720° — one more side, one more 180°: 540 + 180 = 720.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the concentration of salt in solution Z.

The student used a method involving osmosis. The student used tubing made of partially permeable membrane.

This is the method used.

  1. Cut six pieces of tubing to the same length.
  2. Tie one end of each piece of tubing.
  3. Put the same volume of solution Z into each piece of tubing.
  4. Tie the other end of each piece of tubing to form a sealed tube.
  5. Record the mass of each tube.
  6. Place each tube into a different concentration of salt solution.
  7. After 2 hours, remove each tube from the salt solutions.
  8. Record the mass of each tube.

Figure 1 shows one of the sealed tubes in a salt solution: a beaker holding the salt solution, with the sealed tube lying in it, tied at both ends. The liquid inside the tube is labelled solution Z and the wall of the tube is labelled the partially permeable membrane.

name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Glucose and fructose are different sugars. Fructose has a much sweeter taste than glucose.

Suggest two reasons why the drinks company uses fructose in the drink rather than using glucose.

Do not refer to sweetness in your answer.
answer: Any two from: less fructose or sugar is needed; it is cheaper to produce or to buy the drink — less sugar tax, or more profit (cheaper on its own is ignored); there is less energy in the drink, so people are more likely to buy it (fewer calories or joules is accepted). “Less sugar is needed so it would be cheaper” scores both marks on its own. “Fructose is sweeter than glucose” is ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Describe how a student could test the drink for sugar.

Give the colour of a positive result.
answer: Add Benedict’s solution and heat; positive: green, yellow, orange, brown or brick red — any appropriate method of heating, and if a temperature is given it must be at least 60 °C; “warm” is ignored. Positive result: green, yellow, orange, brown or brick red (1). The starting colour is ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Describe how a student could test the drink for protein.

Give the colour of a positive result.
answer: Add Biuret reagent; a positive result is mauve or purple — adding Biuret A and Biuret B is accepted, and so is adding potassium or sodium hydroxide solution and copper sulfate solution. Positive result: mauve, purple, lilac or pink-purple (1). The starting colour is ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The human digestive system breaks down protein and fat in the drink.

Describe how protein and fat are digested.

You should include:

  • the enzymes involved
  • where the enzymes are produced.
answer: Protease (stomach, pancreas, small intestine): protein → amino acids; lipase (pancreas, small intestine): fat → fatty acids + glycerol — Level-marked out of 6. Level 2 (4–6) needs the digestion of BOTH fat and protein, each linked to the right type of enzyme. Protein: protease breaks protein down into amino acids; protease is produced in the stomach, in the pancreas and in the small intestine; hydrochloric acid provides the correct pH for protease in the stomach. Fat: lipase breaks fat down into fatty acids and glycerol; lipase is produced by the pancreas and by the small intestine; bile is produced by the liver, released from the gall bladder, emulsifies the fat to give a larger surface area for lipase, and neutralises the acid to provide the correct pH for the enzymes.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html: What type of microorganism causes measles?
answer: A virus

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Vaccinations help reduce the spread of measles.

Suggest two ways the spread of measles can be reduced.

Do not refer to vaccination in your answer.
answer: Any two: isolate the sick, cover coughs and sneezes, wash hands often — Any two from: isolation of people with measles; covering your nose and mouth when you cough or sneeze (wearing face coverings is accepted); frequent handwashing or sanitiser (frequent cleaning of surfaces is accepted). Unqualified “PPE”, “public health education programmes” and “social distancing” are ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Describe how the measles vaccine helps a person to become immune to the measles pathogen.
answer: It holds dead or weakened measles; white blood cells make specific antibodies and memory cells — Any four from: the vaccine or injection contains a dead or inactive measles pathogen (weakened or attenuated is accepted, and so is “contains measles antigens”); white blood cells produce antibodies (lymphocytes or leucocytes are accepted, phagocytes are not); the antibodies produced are specific to the measles pathogen; memory cells are made; on secondary exposure antibodies are produced faster, or in larger quantities. If nothing else scores, “antibodies are produced” is worth 1. Herd immunity and antitoxins are ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Norovirus is a type of virus.

Explain how viruses cause illness.
answer: Viruses enter cells and reproduce inside them, so the cells are damaged or killed — “live or reproduce inside cells” and “inject genetic material into cells” are both accepted — so the cells are damaged or killed (1), or burst open.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Drugs can help to reduce the symptoms of the norovirus infection.

New drugs must go through clinical trials before being licensed for use.

Give three reasons why clinical trials are needed.
answer: To check it is not toxic and its side effects, that it works (efficacy), and the right dosage — that it is not harmful, or to check for side effects (1); to check efficacy — to see whether the drug works, or whether it treats the disease (1); to determine the dosage — how much is needed (1). “To check the interaction with other drugs” is accepted for the third mark; “dangerous” on its own is ignored.

Tick one box.
answer: 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂

Explain why no gas was produced by the plant at 45 °C.
answer: The enzymes are denatured: the active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits — The enzymes in the plant or chloroplast are destroyed — denatured (1) — because the active site changes shape (1). Two other routes score the same two marks: “the active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits”, and “the enzymes are denatured, so the substrate no longer fits”. “The enzymes are killed” and “the cells or plants are denatured” are not accepted; “the plant is dead” is ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
How could the student increase the accuracy of the results?

Tick one box.
answer: Repeat the investigation, measuring the volume of gas to 0.5 cm³
choices: Repeat the investigation, collecting the gas for 24 hours. | Repeat the investigation, measuring the volume of gas to 0.5 cm<sup>3</sup>. | Repeat the investigation using a different aquatic plant. | Repeat the investigation, using temperatures of 5 °C and 50 °C.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A person grows tomatoes in a greenhouse.

The mean temperature of the greenhouse is 15 °C. A heater would keep the temperature of the greenhouse at 25 °C.

Suggest two reasons against using a heater set at 25 °C in the greenhouse.

Do not refer to cost in your answer.
answer: Any two: a glut, another factor limits, 25 °C may not be optimal, heat loss, pollution — Any two from: there may be too many tomatoes to eat or sell (a glut, or all ripening at once); another factor could limit photosynthesis instead; the optimum temperature might be above or below 25 °C; greenhouses are poorly insulated; pollution from the heater (increased carbon dioxide emissions or global warming); an increased rate of transpiration, so more water lost from the plants; an increased spread of plant disease. If nothing else scores, “it is a fire hazard” is worth 1.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The person cut a stem from one of the tomato plants. The cut stem was placed in soil to grow new roots.

Which tissue in the cut stem will differentiate into new root cells?

Tick one box.
answer: Meristem

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 3 shows bacteria viewed using a microscope. It is a grey, black-and-white image in which several hundred rod-shaped bacteria lie across a fine mesh of fibres. Each rod is separately visible, with its rounded ends and the texture of its own surface showing, and the rods appear to stand out from the surface below them.

What type of microscope was used to view the bacteria in Figure 3?

Give a reason for your answer.
answer: An electron microscope, because it has a high resolution or a high magnification — Both halves are needed for the single mark.
examiner_note: Figure 3 is a third-party photograph — AQA publishes its acknowledgements in a separate booklet — so it cannot be reproduced here; what it shows is described in the question.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Bacterial cells are prokaryotic cells.

Give three ways that a prokaryotic cell is different from a eukaryotic cell.
answer: No nucleus (its DNA is free in the cytoplasm), no mitochondria, and it has plasmids — its DNA or genetic material is free in the cytoplasm; it does not have mitochondria; it has a single loop or strand of DNA; it has plasmids (small rings of DNA); it is smaller (bacteria have smaller ribosomes is accepted). The converse for a eukaryotic cell scores if it is clearly stated. If nothing else scores, “a prokaryotic cell has no membrane-bound organelles” is worth 1. “Genetic information” is ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 4 shows a special slide used to determine the size of a cell viewed using a microscope.

Figure 4 is the circular field of view of the microscope. One cell — a rounded head with a long thin tail — lies across the top of it. Below the cell runs the scale on the slide, numbered 20, 30, 40 and 50, with ten small divisions between one number and the next. A dashed line dropped from each end of the cell meets the scale at 20 and at 50. Printed beside the field of view is: ‘Each small division on the scale is 1.5 µm’.

Calculate the magnification of the cell shown in Figure 4.
answer: × 800 — Measure the cell on the printed page: 36 mm (anything from 35 to 37 mm, or 3.5 to 3.7 cm, is accepted) (1). Convert: 36 × 1000 = 36 000 µm (1). Real size: the cell covers 30 divisions, so 30 × 1.5 = 45 µm (1). Substitute: magnification = 36 000 ÷ 45 (1). Answer 800, with no unit (1). If nothing else scores, writing magnification = image size ÷ real size, or a correct rearrangement, is worth 1.
examiner_note: Figure 4 is artwork in the PDF and is deliberately NOT redrawn: the scheme’s first mark is the cell measured with a ruler on the printed page, which comes to 36 mm at true A4 scale (measured off the PDF’s own coordinates: the 20 and 50 ticks are 102.1 pt apart). A drawing here lays out at whatever width the screen gives it, so measuring it would produce a real number and a wrong answer. The 36 mm above is the scheme’s own figure.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 5 shows a lung cell dividing. It is four drawings in a row, joined by arrows. In the first, the cell holds a tangle of long thin threads. In the second, the threads have become separate short structures, each one doubled along its length. In the third, they have been gathered into two groups, one at each end of the cell. In the fourth, the cell has become two cells side by side, each holding a rounded body with a tangle of threads inside it.

Describe the process of the cell cycle shown in Figure 5.
answer: DNA replicates; the chromosomes are pulled apart; the nucleus, then the cell, divides into two — The DNA replicates, so two copies of each chromosome form (1); one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell (1); the nucleus divides — two new nuclei form (1); the cytoplasm or cell membrane divides and two genetically identical cells form (1). A maximum of 3 marks if the stages are given out of order, and 1 mark for “mitosis” if nothing else scores. “DNA reproduces” is not accepted; the names of the phases of mitosis are ignored.
examiner_note: Figure 5 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed; what the four drawings show is described in the question.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Lung cancer is malignant.

Explain what is meant by a malignant tumour.
answer: Uncontrolled growth that invades nearby tissue and spreads in the blood or lymph — Uncontrolled cell division or growth (1); it invades neighbouring tissues (1); tumour cells spread to different parts of the body, or to other tissues, in the blood or lymph (1) — “the tumour metastasises” is accepted for the third mark.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Smoking can damage the lungs in different ways.

Figure 6 shows alveoli from the lungs of two people. Person A, who does not smoke, has an alveolus drawn as an outline with about ten deep, narrow folds running all the way round it, like the petals of a flower. Person B, who does smoke, has an alveolus of the same overall width drawn with only shallow, rounded waves round its edge.

Person A and person B do the same exercise.

Explain why person B breathes much faster than person A during the exercise.
answer: B breathes faster: a smaller surface area lets less oxygen into the blood for respiration — Person B needs to breathe faster or deeper to get more oxygen (1); because there is a smaller surface area (1); so less oxygen enters the blood — less oxygenation of haemoglobin (1); so there is less oxygen for respiration (1). The converse, clearly stated for person A, scores. “Less energy produced, made or created” is not accepted; “so anaerobic respiration increases”, “so lactic acid is produced” and “so an oxygen debt is created” are accepted for the fourth mark.
examiner_note: Figure 6 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed; the shape of each alveolus is described in the question.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Angina is a condition many people get as coronary heart disease (CHD) develops.

Angina can cause chest pain and tiredness.

People with angina are sometimes treated with a drug called GTN. GTN widens the coronary arteries.

Explain:

  • the causes and symptoms of angina
  • how GTN reduces the symptoms of angina.
answer: Fatty diet, smoking, no exercise: fatty deposits narrow coronary arteries, less oxygen to heart muscle; GTN widens them — Level-marked out of 6. Level 3 (5–6) needs all three of the causes of angina, an explanation of its symptoms, and the treatment with GTN; Level 1 needs the symptoms or the treatment. Causes of angina and CHD: high cholesterol or fat in the blood or diet, obesity; a lack of exercise; smoking or alcohol; increasing age; a family history of atherosclerosis or heart problems. Symptoms: fatty deposits form in the coronary arteries, which narrow, so less blood — and so less oxygen and glucose — reaches the heart muscle and the body; less oxygen and glucose for respiration, so less energy is released, more anaerobic respiration, lactic acid formed, muscle fatigue. GTN: more blood reaches the heart muscle, so more oxygen and glucose reach it, so aerobic respiration increases.

Limpets are small animals with shells.

Limpets attach to rocks on sea shores.

Rat populations can increase rapidly.

When rat populations are large there is competition between rats.

Otters are mammals that live in river ecosystems.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Limpets eat algae.

Limpets are prey for crabs.

Give the food chain for algae, crabs and limpets.
answer: algae → limpets → crabs — algae are the producer, limpets eat the algae and crabs eat the limpets; each arrow points from the food to what eats it, so the direction matters.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Students estimated the population of limpets on a sea shore.

The students were given a square quadrat.

Figure 2 shows the quadrat.

Calculate the area of the quadrat in m2.
answer: 0.25 m² — 50 cm × 50 cm = 2500 cm², and 2500 ÷ (100 × 100) = 0.25 m². ¼ m² is accepted. Converting first scores both marks the same way: 50 ÷ 100 = 0.5 m, then 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25 m².

name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The total area of the sea shore was 1800 m2.

The students sampled 2% of the total area of the sea shore.

Calculate the number of times the students needed to use the quadrat for the 2% sample.

Use your answer from Question 01.2
answer: 144 quadrats — 1800 × <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub> = 36 m², and 36 ÷ 0.25 = 144. 1800 × 0.02 = 36 and 36 × 4 = 144 are both accepted, and so is a correct number of quadrats worked from an incorrect 2% of 1800.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Explain why throwing a quadrat is not a random method to estimate population size.

Do not refer to safety in your answer.
answer: Where it lands is biased (students aim for or avoid the limpets), so the sample is not representative — The location of the sample will be biased or chosen — students may aim for the limpets, aim to avoid them, or stand or start near a group of them — or it will be limited by how far the students can throw. So the results will not be representative of the actual abundance, and the population size will come out too high or too low.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe one method the students could use to plan where the quadrat should be randomly placed each time.
answer: Lay tape measures along two perpendicular sides as axes and use a random number generator for the co-ordinates — or allocate co-ordinates to it, or divide the area into a grid — and then use a random number generator. A description of generating random numbers, such as pulling them out of a container, is accepted. Throwing the quadrat is not.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Suggest one hazard the students should be aware of when collecting data on the sea shore.

Do not refer to throwing quadrats in your answer.
answer: Any one: the sea or tide, slippery rocks, quicksand, glass or needles, sewage, crabs or jellyfish — Any one of: the water, the sea or the waves; the tide; the rocks, or slippery or uneven surfaces; quicksand; a named hazardous material on the sea shore such as needles or glass; sewage; an animal, named — a crab or a jellyfish.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Populations of limpets are monitored to assess the impact of pollution in water.

Suggest one type of pollution in water that may affect the population of limpets.
answer: Any one of: fertiliser, sewage, or a named toxic chemical such as a pesticide or crude oil — a named one such as a herbicide, pesticide, insecticide, DDT or crude oil. Microplastics, dissolved carbon dioxide, heavy metals and thermal pollution are all accepted.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Potato plants are classified as eukaryota.

What type of classification group is eukaryota?

Tick one box.
answer: Domain

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Potato plants can reproduce by asexual reproduction.

Which statement is true for asexual reproduction?

Tick one box.
answer: Offspring are genetically identical
choices: Meiosis occurs. | Offspring are genetically identical. | Pollen and egg cells are produced.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Flowers of potato plants contain gametes for sexual reproduction.

How is a gamete different from other cells in a potato plant?

Tick one box.
answer: A gamete contains half of the number of chromosomes
choices: A gamete contains one-quarter of the number of chromosomes. | A gamete contains half of the number of chromosomes. | A gamete contains double the number of chromosomes.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Plants in the same genus as potatoes have been studied by scientists.

Describe one way a new plant species could be identified as being in the same genus as potatoes.
answer: Any one of: it has a similar or the same structure, characteristics or phenotype as potatoes — a named one such as the same shape, leaves, flowers or taste, or studied with microscopes; similar DNA or genes, by DNA analysis or analysis of genetic material; similar or the same biochemistry; the same first part of the binomial name. ‘Looks the same’ unqualified is ignored, and the SAME DNA or genes is not accepted.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Scientists have collected and stored seeds from species in the same genus as potatoes.

In the future, these seeds may be used for genetic modification of potato plants.

Genetically modified potato plants could help supply food to the human population as the climate changes.

Explain why genetic modification of crop plants may be important for the human population to survive climate change.
answer: Climate change will stop current crops growing; GM could make crops that survive the new conditions — Level-marked out of 6, and for Level 3 the answer must explain an effect of climate change AND a benefit of GM, with a logical link between them. Effects of climate change: it will change weather patterns; it causes flooding, drought or temperature change; farming land is decreased by sea level rise, flooding or desertification; current crops cannot grow or survive in the changed conditions. Benefits of GM: crops may grow in a wider range of conditions; they may resist a wider range of pests and diseases; they may store for longer; yield or growth rate may increase — which feeds an increasing human population, is useful if less land is available for farming, and matters because a larger population needs more land for housing. Also creditable: variation among current crops is reduced by asexual reproduction or selective breeding, and the rate of evolution by natural selection may be slower than the rate of climate change.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe how Figure 3 shows that the allele for AKU is recessive.
answer: The parents of a child who has AKU do not have AKU themselves — A and B do not have AKU but their child D does, and F and G do not have AKU but their children K and L do. ‘Children with AKU have parents who are carriers’ is also accepted.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Which person is definitely heterozygous for AKU?

Tick one box.
answer: G

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A female who has AKU and a male who is heterozygous for AKU plan to have a child.

Determine the probability that the child will have AKU.

You should:

  • complete Figure 4
  • identify the phenotype of each offspring genotype
  • use the symbols: A = dominant allele, a = recessive allele.
answer: 0.5: gametes a, a (female) and A, a (male) give Aa, Aa, aa, aa; Aa does not have AKU, aa has AKU — and 50%, ½, 1 in 2, 1:1 and 50:50 are all accepted; 1:2 and 50/50 are not. The parental gametes are a and a from the female and A and a from the male (1 mark each, and 1 mark if the two are the other way round). The offspring derived from them are Aa, Aa, aa and aa (1). The phenotypes are Aa = no AKU and aa = AKU (1). The probability must match the offspring genotypes the student actually derived.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A mutation is a change in a gene.

People who have AKU have a mutation that causes the production of a non-functioning enzyme.

Enzymes are proteins.

Suggest how a mutation can result in the production of a non-functioning enzyme.
answer: It changes the amino acid sequence, so the enzyme’s active site has a different shape and the substrate cannot bind — The mutation causes an incorrect sequence of amino acids, which causes the enzyme — or its active site — to be a different shape, so the enzyme and the substrate cannot bind. ‘The enzyme is denatured’ is ignored, and ‘no enzyme is produced’ is not accepted.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Some people have In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) treatment to increase the chance of becoming pregnant.

Describe how the process of IVF can result in pregnancy.
answer: FSH and LH injected to mature eggs; eggs fertilised in a lab; the egg divides into an embryo; embryo put in the uterus — The collected eggs are fertilised in the laboratory — fused with sperm, or sperm injected into the egg (1). The fertilised egg undergoes mitosis, dividing to form an embryo (1). One or two embryos, or balls of cells, are inserted into the uterus (1).

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Embryos can be screened to detect inherited disorders.

Give two arguments against embryo screening.

Do not refer to religion in your answer.
answer: Any two: risk to the embryo or mother, stress, the embryo destroyed, cost, no consent — Any two of: a risk to the embryo, including a risk of miscarriage; a risk to the female or mother; it is a stressful process; it may lead to termination of the pregnancy or destruction of the embryo; the high cost of the screening process; the embryo cannot give consent — which extends to increased prejudice against other people with inherited disorders. A risk to the embryo from radiation is not accepted, and references to religion or ethics are ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
When rats compete, the basal metabolic rate of the rats increases.

Basal metabolic rate is controlled in the same way in humans and in rats.

Describe how basal metabolic rate is increased.
answer: More thyroxine is secreted or released (1), from the thyroid gland (1) — The alternative answer is that more adrenaline is secreted or released (1), from the adrenal gland (1).

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The size of a rat population can increase quickly.

One female rat and one male rat can produce 20 offspring every 2 months.

Warfarin is a poison that has been used to control rat populations.

Rat populations can become resistant to warfarin by the process of evolution.

A population of rats was given warfarin for 4 months.

Table 1 shows information about resistance to warfarin in the rat population for a year after warfarin was first given.

Number of months since warfarin was first givenWas warfarin being given?Percentage (%) of rat population resistant to warfarin
0Yes1
2Yes24
4Yes81
6No99
8No92
10No85
12No70

Rats with resistance to warfarin have a smaller mean mass than rats that are not resistant to warfarin.

Smaller rats are often at a disadvantage when competing against larger rats.

Explain the trends in the data when warfarin was being given and when warfarin was no longer given.

Use Table 1.
answer: Resistance rose while warfarin killed non-resistant rats, then fell slowly once it stopped — Level-marked out of 6, and for Level 3 the answer must explain both the increase and the decrease. Trends: the percentage resistant increased for 6 months, or increased while warfarin was being given, then decreased after it stopped; the decrease is slower than the increase; and the change from increase to decrease is not instant at 6 months. The increase: some rats have alleles for resistance, from random mutation, so they are more likely to survive while warfarin is being used; they reproduce and pass the allele to the next generation, repeating for several generations until most of the population is resistant — and several generations fit inside 6 months. The decrease: with warfarin no longer used, resistant rats are outcompeted for food, mates, territory or shelter by non-resistant rats, or are killed by larger non-resistant rats, so rats without resistance become more likely to reproduce.

answer: A community of living things interacting with the non-living parts of their environment — The interaction of a community of living organisms with the non-living parts of their environment or habitat. ‘The interaction of a community of biotic parts and the abiotic parts of their environment’ is accepted.

Otters are an important species for the stability of the river community.

Describe two ways animal species may be important for the stability of a whole community.
answer: Any two: a predator controls its prey, prey feeds a predator, it shapes the habitat, it spreads seeds — Any two of: it may be a predator and so control the prey population, or keep it fairly constant; it may be prey and so provide energy to a predator; it may be a primary consumer and so control the plant or algae population; it may alter the habitat for other species to survive in; it may provide shelter for other species; it may maintain biodiversity; it may disperse seed or pollen. ‘Prey provide food to a predator’ is ignored — the mark is for energy.

  • eat mainly fish.

Explain how the decrease in the concentration of dissolved oxygen in the river water will affect the population of otters.
answer: The otter population falls: fish need oxygen to respire, so fewer fish survive and otters have less food — The decrease in oxygen concentration causes a decrease in the number of fish — more fish die (1) — because fish need oxygen to respire aerobically (1); invertebrates needing oxygen, with fish eating the invertebrates, is accepted. So the otter population decreases because there is less food (1), or its rate of reproduction is lower through lack of food, or the otters migrate to another river. The alternative answer is that the decrease means more bacteria are present (1), so more fish die of bacterial infection (1), so the otter population decreases (1). Implying that otters take oxygen from the water is not accepted, and nor is energy being produced by respiration.

name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Scientists investigated whether blood glucose concentration affects reaction time.

The reaction times of ten people with Type 1 diabetes were measured.

This is the method used.

  1. Tell one person to drink a glucose solution.
  2. Monitor the person’s blood glucose concentration.
  3. Record the person’s reaction time when the person’s blood glucose concentration is: 16 mmol/dm3, 6 mmol/dm3, 3 mmol/dm3.
  4. Repeat steps 1 to 3 for the nine other people.

People with Type 1 diabetes were selected for the investigation instead of people who did not have diabetes.

Explain why.
answer: They make little or no insulin, so their blood glucose varies more and goes very high: a wider range to test — it increases and decreases more, and goes very high, which gives a sufficient range of concentrations to test (1). That is because less or no insulin is produced when the blood glucose concentration increases, so there is nothing to bring it back down (1). The converse, clearly describing people who do not have diabetes, is accepted.

Figure 6 shows the results. The vertical line at each blood glucose concentration is the range of the ten reaction times and the × is their mean.

People who do not have diabetes usually have a blood glucose concentration in the range of 4.0 mmol/dm3 to 7.8 mmol/dm3.

Describe how the results in Figure 6 show the importance of homeostasis.

Homeostasis keeps the blood glucose concentration in a narrow range; alternatively, a lower reaction time is a survival advantage (1).

subject: Combined Science
name: Biology Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe how blood glucose concentration is maintained within narrow limits in people who do not have diabetes.
answer: High: pancreas releases insulin, glucose stored in liver and muscle as glycogen. Low: glucagon turns glycogen to glucose — when it is high, or nears 7.8 mmol/dm³ — the pancreas releases insulin (1). Insulin causes glucose to move from the blood into the liver or muscle cells (1), where the excess glucose is converted to glycogen (1). When the blood glucose concentration decreases — when it is low, or nears 4.0 mmol/dm³ — the pancreas releases glucagon (1), which causes glycogen to be converted into glucose and released into the blood (1). If neither of the two middle marks is earned, ‘glucose moves into cells’ scores 1.

An electrical signal is accepted for an impulse throughout; ‘signal’ or ‘message’ alone is ignored.

name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024

A 5.25 g sample of an alloy of copper and zinc contains 13.5% zinc by mass.

Calculate the mass of copper in the 5.25 g sample. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
answer: 4.54 g — The copper is 100 − 13.5 = 86.5%, so the mass of copper is (86.5 ÷ 100) × 5.25 = 4.54125 g, which is 4.54 g to 3 significant figures. The scheme takes the other route for the same marks: the zinc is (13.5 ÷ 100) × 5.25 = 0.70875 g, so the copper is 5.25 − 0.70875 = 4.54125 g.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 2 shows diagrams which represent the structures of two substances.

Sodium chloride, NaCl is drawn as a packed block of spheres of two sizes, the larger ones each marked − and the smaller ones each marked +, alternating in every direction. Oxygen, O2 is drawn as two circles of the same size joined to each other.

Compare the structure and bonding of sodium chloride and oxygen.
answer: Both have strong bonds; NaCl is a giant ionic lattice, oxygen small covalent molecules — Level marked out of 6. Level 2 (4–6) needs a comparison of either the structure or the bonding of both substances, with a description of magnitude. Indicative content — similarities: both have strong bonds; the particles have full outer shells. Differences: sodium chloride is a compound made from two elements and oxygen is an element; sodium chloride is a giant structure of ions and oxygen is a small molecule; sodium chloride has ionic bonds and consists of oppositely charged ions, with electrons transferred from sodium atoms to chlorine atoms; oxygen is covalent, its molecules made of oxygen atoms joined by a double covalent bond with electrons shared between them, and with weak forces between the molecules.

name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The equation for the reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen to produce ammonia is:

N2 + 3 H2 → 2 NH3

Calculate the mass of hydrogen that is needed to produce 25 g of ammonia.

Relative atomic masses (Ar): H = 1, N = 14
answer: 4.41 g — Mᵣ of NH₃ = 14 + (3 × 1) = 17; moles of NH₃ = 25 ÷ 17 = 1.47; moles of H₂ = 1.47 × <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> = 2.205; mass of H₂ = 2.205 × 2 = 4.41 g. 4.4117647 correctly rounded to at least 2 significant figures is accepted. The scheme's other route scores the same 4 marks: 2 × Mᵣ(NH₃) = 34, so 6 g of H₂ gives 34 g of NH₃, and (6 ÷ 34) × 25 = 4.41 g.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 7 shows the displayed formulae equation for the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen:

N ≡ N + 3 H — H → 2 (H — N(— H) — H)

In the reaction the energy released forming new bonds is 93 kJ/mol greater than the energy needed to break existing bonds.

Table 3 shows bond energies.

BondN ≡ NH — HN — H
Bond energy in kJ/mol945X391

Calculate the bond energy X for the H — H bond. Use Figure 7 and Table 3.
answer: 436 kJ/mol — Bonds broken = 945 + 3X. Bonds made = 6 × 391 = 2346. Energy released = bonds made − bonds broken, so 93 = 2346 − (945 + 3X), giving 3X = 1308 and X = 436.

topics: Bonding & Structure, Atomic Structure & the Periodic Table

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Calcium reacts with chlorine to produce calcium chloride.

Explain what happens to calcium atoms and to chlorine atoms when calcium reacts with chlorine to produce calcium chloride.
answer: Each Ca atom gives two electrons, one to each of two Cl atoms: Ca²⁺ and 2 Cl⁻ — Each calcium atom loses two electrons; each chlorine atom gains one electron; so one calcium atom reacts with two chlorine atoms; forming Ca²⁺ ions and Cl⁻ ions (calcium ions and chloride ions, or ions with full outer shells). 'Calcium atoms lose electrons and chlorine atoms gain electrons' on its own scores 1 of the 4.
topics: Bonding & Structure, Atomic Structure & the Periodic Table

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Explain why chlorine is more reactive than bromine.
answer: Its outer shell is nearer the nucleus, so it attracts an electron more strongly — Chlorine has fewer shells (chlorine is a smaller atom), so the outer shell is closer to the nucleus (there is less shielding), so there is a stronger attraction between the nucleus and the electron gained, so it gains the electron more easily. The converse argued for bromine is accepted throughout, and 'energy level' is accepted for 'shell'.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024

Hydrogen halideBoiling point in °C
HF20
HCl−85
HBr−67
HI−35

Describe how the boiling points of the hydrogen halides change as the relative formula mass changes.
answer: Boiling point increases as relative formula mass increases, except HF, which has the highest boiling point — but HF has the highest boiling point (HF does not follow the trend, or HF is anomalous).
topics: Atomic Structure & the Periodic Table, Bonding & Structure

subject: Combined Science

answer: Hexagonal rings of carbon atoms

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Nanotubes are used in electronics.

Give one other use of nanotubes.
answer: Any one of: drug delivery, or in materials such as sporting equipment or body armour — a suitable use such as sporting equipment or body armour; drug delivery. References to electronic use are ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A nanotube contains 2380 carbon atoms.

Calculate the number of moles of carbon in this nanotube.

The Avogadro constant is 6.02 × 1023 per mole.
answer: 3.95 × 10⁻²¹ mol — the number of moles is 2380 ÷ (6.02 × 10²³) = 3.953488 × 10⁻²¹, and an answer correctly rounded to at least 2 significant figures is accepted.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Explain why carbon nanotubes can conduct electricity. Refer to bonding between carbon atoms in your answer.
answer: Each carbon makes three bonds, so one electron per atom is delocalised and carries charge — Each carbon atom forms three covalent bonds, so one electron from each carbon atom is delocalised, so these delocalised electrons carry charge through the structure (through the nanotube).

2 SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2 SO3(g)

answer: A molecule made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms only

The general formula for alkanes is CnH2n+2

Determine the formula of the alkane with 10 carbon atoms.
answer: C<sub>10</sub>H<sub>22</sub> — with n = 10, the number of hydrogens is 2 × 10 + 2 = 22

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons.

Figure 1 represents industrial equipment used to separate crude oil into fractions.

Figure 1 is a diagram of the equipment. A pipe labelled Crude oil enters on the left and coils through a furnace, with an arrow labelled Heat pointing up into it from below. From the furnace a pipe runs into the lower part of a tall column. The column is drawn with five trays at different heights, each with an outlet pipe leaving the side of the column, together with one outlet at the very top and one at the very bottom. A long arrow beside the column, pointing upwards, is labelled Decreasing temperature.

Explain how crude oil is separated into fractions. Use Figure 1.
answer: Heated crude oil vaporises; the column is cooler higher up; fractions condense at different heights — Four marks, one each: the crude oil is heated; so some of the hydrocarbons vaporise; the column has a temperature gradient (allow: the column gets cooler going up); so the hydrocarbons or fractions condense at different heights or temperatures in the column — or, for the same mark, they condense at their boiling points.
examiner_note: Figure 1 is a raster image inside the PDF with no text layer, so it is described in the question rather than reproduced. Every label it carries, including the upward 'Decreasing temperature' arrow, is transcribed, because the paper hands those to the student.

subject: Combined Science

The alkane molecule C14H30 can be cracked to produce smaller molecules.

Balance the equation for the reaction.

C14H30 → C8H18 + ......... C3H6
answer: C14H30 → C8H18 + 2 C3H6 — carbon: 8 + 2 × 3 = 14, and hydrogen: 18 + 2 × 6 = 30

Propene (C3H6) is an alkene.

Describe the test for alkenes. Give the result.
answer: Add bromine water: orange to colourless — Test: add bromine water. Result: it changes from orange to colourless (allow: it decolourises; ignore 'clear'). The result mark is dependent on the test mark being awarded.

What type of substance is poly(propene)?
answer: A polymer (allow: plastic; allow: hydrocarbon)

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the effect of changing the particle size of calcium carbonate on the rate of reaction with hydrochloric acid.

Figure 3 shows the apparatus, with these parts labelled: a conical flask holding hydrochloric acid, with pieces of calcium carbonate lying at the bottom and bubbles rising through the liquid; a stopper in the neck of the flask carrying a delivery tube; and that delivery tube running across and up into an inverted measuring cylinder standing in a trough of water, with carbon dioxide collecting in the closed top of the cylinder.

Describe a method the student could use to produce valid results.
answer: Time the gas from the same acid with different sizes of calcium carbonate chips — Level-marked out of 6. Level 3 (5–6) the method would lead to a valid outcome, key steps identified and logically sequenced; Level 2 (3–4) not necessarily valid, most steps identified but not fully sequenced; Level 1 (1–2) some relevant steps, links not clear. Indicative content: measure a volume of hydrochloric acid using a measuring cylinder; measure a mass of calcium carbonate using a balance; add the acid to the calcium carbonate in the conical flask; put the stopper and delivery tube into the flask; start a timer; record the volume of gas collected at set time intervals, or time how long it takes for a fixed volume of gas to be collected; repeat using different sized pieces of calcium carbonate; keep the same mass of calcium carbonate, the same volume, concentration and temperature of acid; repeat each experiment.
examiner_note: Figure 3 is a raster image inside the PDF; its labelled parts are transcribed into the question, because the student is told the apparatus is shown and the labels are what the method is written from.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The student investigated the effect of increasing the temperature on the rate of a reaction.

Explain the effect of increasing the temperature on the rate of a reaction. Refer to particles and collisions in your answer.
answer: The rate increases: faster particles collide more often, and more often with enough energy — Three marks, one each: increasing the temperature increases the rate of reaction; because the particles have more energy (allow: the particles move faster); so the frequency of collisions increases (allow: a greater proportion of collisions have enough energy to react).

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Catalysts affect the rate of reactions.

What is meant by a ‘catalyst’?
answer: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up — A substance that increases the rate of reaction (allow: changes the rate of reaction), and is not used up during the reaction. 'Does not take part in the reaction' is ignored.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html: What are catalysts in biological systems called?
answer: Enzymes

subject: Combined Science

html: Some fractions of crude oil are processed to produce fuel for transport.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe how crude oil was formed.
answer: Dead plankton buried in mud and compressed over millions of years — Four marks, one each: plankton died (allow: the remains of ancient biomass); and were buried in mud (allow: buried by sediments); and were compressed; over millions of years.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Transport is a source of atmospheric pollutants.

Suggest how sulfur dioxide can be produced by transport.
answer: Sulfur in the fuel reacts with oxygen when it burns — Some fuels contain sulfur (a named fossil fuel is allowed for 'fuels'); which reacts with oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Give two problems caused by sulfur dioxide as an atmospheric pollutant.
answer: Acid rain, and breathing problems such as asthma — Acid rain (allow a specific effect of acid rain); and respiratory problems in humans (allow a named respiratory problem, for example asthma).

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe how carbon monoxide can be produced by transport.
answer: Fuel burning in too little oxygen (incomplete combustion) — Fuels are burnt (a named fossil fuel is allowed); in insufficient or limited oxygen (allow: carbon monoxide is produced by incomplete combustion).

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Catalytic converters are fitted to car exhausts to reduce the amount of pollution from cars.

Carbon monoxide and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) react in a catalytic converter. Nitrogen and carbon dioxide are produced.

Write a balanced equation for the reaction.
answer: 4 CO + 2 NO<sub>2</sub> → N<sub>2</sub> + 4 CO<sub>2</sub> — carbon 4 = 4, oxygen 4 + 4 = 8, nitrogen 2 = 2. CO + NO<sub>2</sub> → N<sub>2</sub> + CO<sub>2</sub> with no balancing numbers, or with incorrect ones, scores 1 of the 2.

subject: Combined Science
name: Chemistry Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain why the red colour did not move from the start line.
answer: The red colour is insoluble in the solvent; so it does not move with the solvent.

Calculate the distance moved by the solvent.

subject: Combined Science

There were four colours in the printer ink.
