Table 2 shows data about the EHT and the Hubble telescope.

ApertureOperating wavelength
EHT1.3 × 107 m1.3 mm

Galaxy M87 is 5.3 × 107 light years from Earth. The supermassive black hole at the centre of M87 has a mass 6.5 × 109 times the mass of the Sun.

The radius of the event horizon is R.

The astronomers propose to use either the EHT or the Hubble telescope to observe stars whose distance from the centre of the black hole is less than 1000R.

Discuss, with calculations, which telescope is more suitable for this observation.
answer: The EHT — R<sub>s</sub> = 2GM/c² = 2 × 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 6.5 × 10⁹ × 1.99 × 10³⁰ / (3 × 10⁸)² = 1.9 × 10¹³ m (1). The region subtends 1.917 × 10¹³ × 2 × 1000 / (5.3 × 10⁷ × 9.46 × 10¹⁵) = 7.6 × 10⁻⁸ rad (1; 3.8 × 10⁻⁸ without the 2 is condoned). Resolution of the EHT = 1.3 × 10⁻³ / 1.3 × 10⁷ = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ rad, or of Hubble = 410 × 10⁻⁹ / 2.4 = 1.71 × 10⁻⁷ rad (1). Both resolutions correct and the conclusion that the EHT is better than Hubble (1). Alternative: the smallest size each can resolve at the distance of M87 is 5.0 × 10¹³ m for the EHT and 8.6 × 10¹⁶ m for Hubble. Rounding errors are condoned.

html:
M40 A and M40 B are two stars that appear very close to each other when viewed from Earth.

There are two possible reasons for this:

  • they are an orbiting binary system
  • they are distant from each other and only appear in the same line of sight.

In an orbiting binary system, the difference between the apparent magnitude and the absolute magnitude for each star is similar.

Table 3 shows data about these two stars.

Temperature / KRadius of star / mApparent magnitude
M40 A60006.3 × 1099.7
M40 B47001.1 × 101010.1

Discuss the appearance of the two stars to an astronomer on the Earth.

In your answer you should:

  • compare the colour of the stars
  • compare the brightness of the stars
  • deduce, with a calculation, whether the stars form an orbiting binary system.
answer: M40 B looks redder (cooler) and M40 A brighter; not a binary, as A emits less power yet looks brighter, so it is closer — Level-marked out of 6: 6 — all three areas covered, at least two in some detail; 5 — two areas successful and one partial; 3–4 — two areas successful, or one successful and others partial; 1–2 — one area. Colour: M40 B appears more red than M40 A because it is cooler; M40 A is an F/G star (white / yellow-white) and M40 B a K-class star (orange). Brightness: M40 A appears brighter, its apparent magnitude being 0.4 less; the ratio is 2.51<sup>0.4</sup> = 1.5. Binary: using P = σAT⁴, P<sub>A</sub> = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 4π × (6.3 × 10⁹)² × 6000⁴ = 3.66 × 10²⁸ W and P<sub>B</sub> = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 4π × (1.1 × 10¹⁰)² × 4700⁴ = 4.22 × 10²⁸ W. A has the lower power output yet appears brighter, so A must be closer — they are not a binary.

Using H = 65 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ is not accepted unless it is obtained from the gradient.

Bill is a builder.

He used 24 kg of sand and 5 kg of cement.

On Tuesday Bill will make the same type of mortar mix.
He will use 36 kg of sand.

How much cement does he need to make the same type of mortar mix?
name: Practice paper 1, Section A: Non-calculator (September 2019 materials)
subject: Maths
answer: 7.5 kg — 36 kg of sand is one and a half times 24 kg, so the cement is one and a half times 5 kg: 5 × 1.5 = 7.5. (Or 5 ÷ 24 × 36, or 12 kg of sand takes 2.5 kg of cement and 36 is three twelves.)

subject: Maths
topics: Percentage of an Amount, Percentage Increase & Decrease
answer: No: her profit is 2 × £22 + £20 − £50 = £14, which is 28% of £50, not over 30% — She takes 2 × £22 + £20 = £64, so her profit is £64 − £50 = £14. 30% of £50 is £15, and £14 is less than that — or £14 ÷ £50 = 28%, which is not over 30%. The marks are for the figures, not the word.

html: Will the area of the development be greater than the total area of 50 football pitches?
name: Practice paper 1, Section A: Non-calculator (September 2019 materials)
subject: Maths
answer: Yes: the triangle is 1⁄2 × 800 × 800 = 320 000 m2, more than 50 × 5000 = 250 000 m2 — Half a mile is 800 m, so the triangle is 1⁄2 × 800 × 800 = 320 000 m2. One pitch is 100 × 50 = 5000 m2, so 50 pitches are 250 000 m2, and 320 000 is more. (In square miles: the triangle is 1⁄8 of a square mile.) Forgetting the half gives 640 000 and the right word for the wrong reason.

html:
One day

  • Anaya used 44 litres of fuel
  • Meera used 8 gallons of fuel.

Anaya used more fuel than Meera.

Use the graph to work out how much more.
Remember to give units with your answer.
name: Practice paper 1, Section B: Calculator (September 2019 materials)
subject: Maths
answer: About 8 litres (or about 1.7 gallons) — 8 gallons reads as about 36 litres, and 44 − 36 = 8; or 44 litres reads as about 9.7 gallons, and 9.7 − 8 = 1.7. Either is right only WITH its unit. There is no mark scheme in Drive for this paper, so this answer is worked here and marked by a person.

html:
David reads this advert on his county council website.

70% of the area of woodland in the county is native woodland.

This means there are 350 km2 of native woodland in the county.

Work out the area of woodland in the county that is not native woodland.
name: Practice paper 1, Section B: Calculator (September 2019 materials)
subject: Maths
answer: 150 km2 — 350 is 70%, so 10% is 50 and the other 30% is 150. (Or the whole is 350 ÷ 0.7 = 500, and 500 − 350 = 150.) 30% of 350 = 105 is the trap.

html: Describe how the student could measure the volume of the piece of rock.

name: Particle Model of Matter: Density
subject: Physics
html: Give one source of error that may have occurred when the student measured the volume of the rock.
answer: Eye not level with the water when reading the cylinder — or the can not filled to the spout at the start, or not all the displaced water collected.

name: Particle Model of Matter: Density
subject: Physics
html: How would the error you described in part (d) affect the measured volume of the rock?
answer: The measured volume would be too low or too high — the direction must match the error given in (d): e.g. water not all collected makes the volume too low.

A student wants to calculate the density of the two objects shown in the figure.

Describe the methods that the student should use to calculate the densities of the two objects.
diagram: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 190" role="img" aria-label="Two objects: on the left a metal cube with straight edges; on the right a small statue, a carved bust of a head on a stand, with an irregular shape."><g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M40 70 L100 70 L100 130 L40 130 Z"/><path d="M40 70 L62 50 L122 50 L100 70"/><path d="M100 130 L122 110 L122 50"/><ellipse cx="250" cy="48" rx="17" ry="21"/><path d="M243 68 Q244 78 236 82 Q214 88 212 104 L288 104 Q286 88 264 82 Q256 78 257 68"/><path d="M236 104 L236 116 L264 116 L264 104"/><path d="M228 116 L272 116 L276 136 L224 136 Z"/></g><text class="lbl" x="81" y="160" text-anchor="middle">Metal cube</text><text class="lbl" x="250" y="160" text-anchor="middle">Small statue</text></svg>
answer: Mass on a balance; volume by ruler (cube) and by displacement (statue); density = mass ÷ volume — cube: measure a side and cube it; statue: lower it into a displacement can and measure the water pushed out. Full marks need both methods in order, with the equation.

subject: Physics
html: Describe the movement of the particles of helium gas inside the balloon.
answer: They move randomly, in all directions, at a range of speeds — one mark for the range of speeds, one for moving in different (random) directions.

name: Particle Model of Matter: Density
subject: Physics
html:
What name is given to the total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles of helium gas in the balloon?

Tick one box.
choices: External energy | Internal energy | Movement energy
answer: Internal energy

name: Particle Model of Matter: Density
subject: Physics
html: Write down the equation which links density, mass and volume.
answer: density = mass ÷ volume (ρ = m/V)

name: Particle Model of Matter: Density
subject: Physics
html:
The helium in the balloon has a mass of 0.00254 kg.
The balloon has a volume of 0.0141 m³.

Calculate the density of helium. Choose the correct unit from: m³/kg, kg/m³, kg m³
answer: 0.18 kg/m³ — density = 0.00254 ÷ 0.0141 = 0.180… Two marks for 0.18, one for the unit kg/m³.
